svg.title: Go Collections vs Java Collections Framework: Architecture and Memory Layout
svg.desc: Architectural comparison of Go's flat composition model and proposed collections with Java's deep object-oriented hierarchy. Details memory layout, iterators, and concurrency.
svg.text: Go Collections vs Java Collections: Architecture and Memory
Orthogonal functions and value layouts versus deep inheritance hierarchies and boxed references.
Memory layout
Go: Contiguous value slices
Java: Arrays of heap pointers
Cache locality & pointer chasing
Hierarchy & design
Go: Orthogonal generic packages
Java: Strict class/interface tree
Composition vs polymorphism
Iteration model
Go 1.23+: Coroutine iter.Seq[V]
Java: java.util.Iterator & Stream
Push-iterators vs stateful pull
Java: Unified object-oriented hierarchy
Iterable <T> ➔ Collection <T> ➔ List / Set / Queue
Separate Map <K,V> key-value hierarchy
Rich concurrent variants: ConcurrentHashMap, BlockingQueue
Streams API with parallel pipeline execution
Cost: Object header overhead (12–16 bytes per element)
Focus: Polymorphism, enterprise abstraction, type safety
Go: Primitives + Composable generic packages
Built-in language runtime types: slice and map
Standalone generic algorithm libraries: slices, maps, cmp
Proposed Go 1.28 standard collections: set, heap, orderedmap
Push-based iteration using iter.Seq closures in for...range
Memory: Inlined contiguous structs without boxing overhead
Focus: Simplicity, hardware cache locality, low GC pressure
Architectural trade-off: Enterprise ergonomics versus mechanical sympathy
Java collections excel when complex business domain models require runtime interface polymorphism and thread-safe queues.
Go collections minimize heap allocations by embedding structs directly in slice buffers, avoiding GC card-table write barriers.
Go's proposed collections standardize idioms (e.g. map[K]struct{} to set.Set[K]) without introducing heavyweight subtyping.
Choose based on data volume, allocation budgets and whether concurrency is coordinated via channels or shared memory.
Source boundary: Java mechanisms follow JDK 21–25 specifications; Go 1.28 collections reflect active GitHub proposal discussions.
Proposed Go package APIs, method names and iterator signatures remain subject to change prior to formal standard library adoption.
Architecture & Design by Srinivasan Ragothaman (@rsrini7)
